title: A string or a `.` chain converts to an html literal through one refactor the language server computes, and no fix-all applies it
scope:
one editor code action, its kind, the VS Code command that applies it, and the boundary that every
other code action is a diagnostic's suggestion. The html literal's grammar and every program's behaviour are
unchanged.
validatedBy:
the unit tests in `crates/nvs-lsp/src/html_literal.rs`,
`the_html_literal_refactor_has_its_own_kind_and_is_never_in_a_fix_all` in `crates/nvs-lsp/tests/actions.rs`,
and the `.lspt` cases under `tests/lsp/actions/` that name `rule:ide/a-string-converts-to-an-html-template`.

summary.headline: The editor converts a string to an html literal
summary.body: Put the cursor on a string, or on a `.` chain such as `"" . $name . ""`, and choose **Convert to html literal**. The editor writes `` html`{$name}` ``, which prints the same text. The text of an html literal is printed as markup, so read the preview before you apply it. The action never runs on save.
